items.topic: Fair Isaac (FICO) -13.15% on wholesale-pricing freeze and FHFA pressure
items.facts: FICO said it will hold its wholesale FICO Score price at $10 for mortgage lenders enrolled in its Preferred partner program, a defensive move against VantageScore's gains under FHFA's new combined mortgage pricing grid (which now treats VantageScore 4.0 and Classic FICO equally, removing VantageScore's prior 20-point pricing deduction). FHFA Director Bill Pulte posted that regulators are 'taking more action this week' on credit-score competition. Wells Fargo downgraded FICO to Equal Weight; UBS cut its target to $942 from $1,100; BMO Capital cut its target to $897. This system's own close: -13.15% to $708.07 from $815.31. Press figures for the day's drop ranged 13.09%-14.49% depending on snapshot timing; this system's own script-verified close is used for magnitude per §4C.
items.caveat: Press cited only for the stated reason and analyst-reaction facts, per §4C; this system's own macro_series.csv/movers scan used for magnitude.

items.topic: Anthropic S-1 IPO filing and the broad AI-chip/semiconductor rally
items.facts: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 prospectus Monday 10-26, planning a Nasdaq listing under the ticker 'ANT'; share count and valuation undetermined at filing. The S-1 disclosed approximately $16.3B in first-half-2026 revenue and a net loss of about $80.7B, of which roughly $72.4B is a non-cash charge tied to revaluing convertible notes (not operating cash burn), per Chartmill's read of the filing. Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron and Intel rose in midday trading; the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) each rose roughly 2.8-3% the same session. This system's own scan shows Lumentum (+8.19%), Texas Instruments, NXP, Analog Devices, Lam Research, AMD, Applied Materials and Micron among the day's gainers riding the same catalyst (data/raw/movers_2026-10-26.json).
items.caveat: Sources disagreed on exact index-level move sizes (Dow +0.4% to S&P 500 +0.7% depending on outlet/snapshot); this system's own SPX/SMH closes (macro_series.csv) used for any index-level magnitude claim. Tesla and Lockheed Martin moves were also reported same-day by Chartmill (single-sourced) as driven by separate analyst upgrades; this system found no second source or a dated-today upgrade for either and does not assert a reason for TSLA/LMT's moves beyond the broad rally already covered via Lumentum.

items.topic: Charter Communications (CHTR) -5.92%, 52-week low amid sector-wide telecom selloff
items.facts: Charter Communications hit a new 52-week low on 10-26 (reported range $101.57-$102.72 depending on snapshot; this system's own close $102.18, -5.92%). Sector peers Vodafone/VSNT and Cable One (CABO) also fell the same session; coverage attributes the move to a sector-wide selloff among telecom service providers rather than a Charter-specific headline. Background context (not dated to today): Charter has faced sustained pressure over 2026 on broadband-subscriber losses and Starlink/satellite competitive fears.
items.caveat: No same-day, Charter-specific catalyst was found; reported as a sector-wide pattern per §4C, consistent with the day's XLC sector-divergence screen hit (movers_2026-10-26.json).
